display_name: Codex AI Game Studio for Windows

limitations: The executable must resolve to a native Windows binary for the detected architecture.
Windows PowerShell 5.1 lacks some PowerShell 7 language and encoding behavior; prefer standard-library Python for shared portable helpers.

package_managers.install_policy: Use only a verified package identifier and exact version recorded in a confirmed transaction.
Use only when the repository, package maintainer, checksum, version, and license are verified in the plan.
Use only a pinned manifest from a verified bucket after confirmation.

limitations: CUDA capability is unverified until the GPU, driver, runtime, required compute capability, and VRAM meet the selected tool's pinned requirements.
DirectML is capability-equivalent for selected inference tools, not a binary replacement for CUDA or Metal, and output/performance must be benchmarked.
CPU execution can be substantially slower and may require reduced model or asset settings.
WARP is a software graphics fallback for validation and is not evidence of acceptable production rendering or inference performance.

read_only_detection: Resolve project markers and existing editor paths without starting Unity or Unity Hub.
Resolve native Godot executables and project version features without importing the project.
Read the project engine association and resolve installed native editors without launching or compiling Unreal.
Resolve the Blender executable and version metadata without opening a scene.
Resolve the licensed native Aseprite installation without opening an asset.
Resolve a native Windows Pixelorama build and architecture without opening an asset.
Resolve the native Tiled executable and project files without loading or rewriting maps.

native_capabilities: Run standard-library Python helpers as native Windows processes.
Run thin PowerShell launchers without nested shell-string evaluation.
Discover game engines, DCC tools, GPU providers, package managers, and existing MCP configuration read-only.
Route each host application to at most one confirmed MCP server.
Create digest-bound setup, disable, and rollback proposals with project-state backups.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: The upstream workflow supplies only a POSIX shell launcher or assumes POSIX paths and process semantics.
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Port the launcher mechanically to standard-library Python or argument-array PowerShell while preserving the pinned source behavior and tests.
alternatives: Use a verified native Windows entrypoint from the same pinned upstream source.
Use a verified capability-equivalent Windows tool with comparable artifacts and quality gates.
Use WSL or a documented manual handoff only after its filesystem, GUI, process, and performance limitations are accepted.
limitations: A port is not accepted until path, quoting, exit-code, signal, encoding, and rollback tests pass on the detected architecture.
POSIX binaries are never labeled as native Windows binaries.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: The workflow depends on a macOS application bundle, Apple framework, or macOS-only automation surface.
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Build or adapt portable upstream source for Windows only when the license, dependency graph, architecture, and upstream tests permit it.
alternatives: Select a verified Windows application that provides the required import, export, automation, and quality capabilities.
Use an interchange-file manual handoff with an explicit artifact contract.
Use a hosted service only after cost, privacy, data retention, rights, and network requirements are confirmed.
limitations: macOS application bundles and Apple frameworks are not binary-compatible with Windows.
Feature names do not establish output-quality or workflow parity; evidence must be captured.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: The documented installation route is Homebrew-only even though the underlying source may be portable.
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Resolve the same pinned upstream release through a verified Windows package, signed release artifact, or reproducible source build.
alternatives: Use winget, Chocolatey, or Scoop only when package identity, publisher, version, checksum, and license match the proposal.
Use a portable archive from the pinned upstream release after checksum verification.
Use a capability-equivalent tool or manual setup after confirmation.
limitations: Matching package names across registries do not prove common provenance.
Unpinned community manifests are not eligible for automatic execution.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: The generation or validation workflow requires Apple Metal or Metal Performance Shaders.
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Route to a verified DirectML, CUDA, or CPU implementation using the same model/version and compatible preprocessing when available.
alternatives: Use CUDA when a compatible NVIDIA GPU, driver, runtime, VRAM budget, license, and deterministic test fixture are verified.
Use DirectML when the selected tool explicitly supports it and representative quality and performance gates pass.
Use CPU, a hosted provider, or a manual cross-machine handoff after confirming performance, privacy, cost, and provenance effects.
limitations: DirectML, CUDA, CPU, and Metal backends are capability routes, not binary-compatible replacements.
Backend changes can alter determinism, precision, memory use, throughput, and output quality.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: The upstream dependency publishes only an Apple-Silicon executable or assumes Apple ARM frameworks.
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Compile portable, licensed source for Windows arm64 or amd64 only when the dependency graph and tests explicitly support that target.
alternatives: Select an upstream Windows build with an immutable pin and verified signature or checksum.
Select a verified capability-equivalent Windows implementation for the detected architecture.
Use a hosted or manual handoff after confirming rights, privacy, cost, output format, and quality limits.
limitations: Apple-Silicon executables cannot run as native Windows arm64 or amd64 executables.
Architecture translation is not proposed as evidence of application, driver, or plugin compatibility.

allowed_for: A verified command-line dependency with no feasible native route and no GUI or editor-control requirement.
A reproducible build or conversion step whose input and output stay on the same WSL filesystem.
not_allowed_for: Direct GUI editor or DCC automation.
Silent access to Windows credentials or MCP configuration.
Cross-boundary project writes without an explicit path, performance, ownership, and rollback review.
disclosures: State the distribution, filesystem boundary, network boundary, process ownership, expected performance, and exact files crossing between WSL and Windows.

sequence: Create one Windows edition plan at the requested plan path.
Present actions, pins, downloads, licenses, permissions, backups, rollback, expiry, and digest.
Wait for the user to repeat the exact SHA-256 digest.
Apply only the unchanged, unexpired plan with the confirmed digest.
Run health checks and issue a transaction receipt.
transaction_contract.confirmation: The user must repeat the displayed digest verbatim; general approval does not authorize apply.
plan_writes: Only the explicitly requested plan output path may be written before confirmation.
pre_confirmation_prohibitions: No package installation, download, editor launch, MCP activation, hook trust, configuration write, model retrieval, or platform substitution.

permissions: Read OS, architecture, PowerShell, package-manager, application, GPU, disk, and network metadata.
Read selected project markers, Git status, existing MCP configuration names, and credential environment-variable names without reading secret values.
After digest confirmation, write only transaction-listed Codex, MCP, project-state, lock, adapter, and editor integration files.
After digest confirmation, spawn only pinned executables with argument arrays and the disclosed filesystem and localhost network scopes.
After digest confirmation, perform only the downloads whose URL, immutable pin, license, expected size, destination, and checksum policy appear in the transaction.
health_checks: Confirm native Windows and the selected amd64 or arm64 architecture.
Recompute hashes for selected executables and reject mismatches.
Confirm exactly one active MCP server for each host application.
Verify selected engine and DCC versions against project markers without destructive import.
Verify the selected CUDA, DirectML, CPU, or WARP route using a representative non-destructive fixture.
Validate .ai-game-studio/project.json and .ai-game-studio/lock.json against the confirmed transaction.
Record evidence paths, remaining limitations, and the transaction ID.
uninstall: Generate edition disable windows as a new digest-bound proposal.
Stop transaction-owned processes and disable transaction-owned MCP entries only after confirmation.
Remove only transaction-owned launchers, adapters, and configuration after backups are verified.
Leave external editors, engines, models, and pre-existing package-manager state untouched unless their removal is separately listed and confirmed.
rollback: Generate edition rollback <transaction-id> as a separate proposal with its own expiry and digest.
Restore .ai-game-studio/project.json, .ai-game-studio/lock.json, MCP configuration, and modified project/editor files from transaction backups.
Restore the previous single-server host selections and environment entries.
Remove only files created by the selected transaction and report files retained because ownership is uncertain.
Run the read-only doctor and health checks again and preserve the rollback receipt.
